note: A general description of electrical and electronic engineering roles. It is not a job description or hiring requirement from any company and is not used for measurement or scoring.

ROLE_DESIGN_V1.summary: Taking a requirement specification, choosing the circuit topology and component values, and getting a real board built from that schematic
ROLE_DESIGN_V1.practiceWhere: in an electronic circuits lab course or your capstone design

TD01.why: Turning a specification into gain, bandwidth and noise figures and setting component values and operating points is the foundation of circuit design.
TD01.ctx: in an electronic circuits lab or a sensor signal amplification project

TD08.why: Choosing the converter topology and switching devices for the power stage matters because almost every board needs a power supply design.
TD08.ctx: in a power electronics lab or when you own the power stage in your capstone

TD02.why: Setting state machines and timing for digital blocks is where design decisions get made at the boundary with the analogue section.
TD02.ctx: in a digital logic design course or FPGA lab

J1.task: Next to the block diagram, write what the board you own in your capstone will and will not do (for example, power comes from an external adapter).
J1.output: Block diagram with a scope note
J1.check: Does it say which functions are left to other blocks?

J2.task: Turn a requirement such as amplify the sensor signal properly into figures for gain, bandwidth, allowable noise and supply current.
J2.check: Does every item have a target value and a tolerance?

J3.task: Calculate the resistor and capacitor values for an amplifier stage or filter by hand, and note the difference introduced when you round to standard values.
J3.check: Are the calculated values and the standard values you picked shown side by side?

J4.task: Check the same circuit two ways, by hand calculation and in a circuit simulator, and decide which result to treat as the reference.
J4.output: Note comparing hand calculation and simulation
J4.check: Where the two values differ, did you write why?

J5.task: Tidy the schematic and parts list so someone else could order the parts and solder the board straight away.
J5.output: Schematic and parts list as one set
J5.check: Does every part have its value, rating and package?

J6.task: Measure the prototype board and compare it with simulation under the same input, load and temperature.
J6.check: Are the comparison conditions written in the table?

J7.task: Take one problem you hit, such as oscillation, saturation or excess noise, narrow it down to component values, layout or power, fix it and measure again.
J7.check: Are the measurements before and after the fix both there?

J8.task: If a teammate built a board or wrote firmware from your schematic, record the questions they asked and what you changed.
J8.check: Does it say who used your schematic and at which stage?

responsibilities: Turning requirements into circuit specifications and choosing the block structure
Drawing schematics, selecting components and writing design calculations
Measuring prototype boards and revising the design
Reviewing PCB layout and handing design data to test and production

process.what: Input and output conditions and performance targets arrive from product planning or the system level above.
You pick the circuit topology and key components, and decide which competing performance target to protect first.
You calculate component values and use simulation to check operating points and frequency response.
You release the schematic and parts list and a prototype board is built.
You compare measurements with design values and fix component values or layout where they disagree.
You pass the final schematic and calculations to test and production and answer their questions.

tools: Circuit simulators (SPICE family)
PCB design tools (schematic capture and layout)
Oscilloscope, function generator and DC power supply
How to read component datasheets
experiences: Designing a circuit yourself from target figures and building it as a board
Finding and fixing the cause when simulation and measurement disagreed
Having someone else carry on work from your schematic
entry: In your electronics lab reports, put hand calculation, simulation and measurement side by side
Take on the power stage or a sensor interface circuit in your capstone design
Get the schematic of an open-source development board and summarise on one page what each block does

learnOrder.why: Component selection starts with reading ratings and absolute limits.
A simulation run without a hand calculation is hard to catch when it is wrong.
You only know whether a design works once you measure the board.
The same schematic can have different noise and heating depending on the layout.

firstProject.title: Design one sensor signal amplifier board
firstProject.goal: Design a circuit that scales the small output of a temperature or light sensor to the input range of a microcontroller, and take it through to measurement
steps: Write down the sensor output range and the ADC input range, and set the gain and bandwidth you need
Calculate the op-amp circuit component values by hand and check them in a simulator
Build the board on stripboard or a small PCB and measure the output while varying the input
Put the design, simulated and measured values in one table and write down why they differ
firstProject.output: Design specification table, schematic and parts list, and a one-page three-way comparison table
firstProject.check: Do the measured values fall within the specification, and if not, can you explain why?

portfolio: A schematic with a component selection table
A design calculation that sets the component values
A comparison table of design values against measured values

interview.q: How did you set the component values? How did you handle the difference when you rounded to standard values?
interview.why: It shows both whether you did the calculation yourself and whether you can carry it into real hardware.

interview.q: Has a circuit ever not worked the way you expected? How did you narrow down the cause?
interview.why: A large part of design work is fixing prototype boards.

interview.q: Has anyone else worked from a schematic you drew?
interview.why: A schematic only counts as a deliverable when someone else can read it and build from it.

postingCheck: Whether hardware design here centres on analogue and power circuits or on digital and board design
Which product line the circuits are for (power supplies, sensors, motor drives, communication modules and so on)
Whether specific design tools or test equipment are listed as a plus
ROLE_DESIGN_V1.watch: Circuit design postings vary a lot with the product. Under the same title, such as Hardware Engineer or Electronics Design Engineer, check first whether the work is closer to power circuits, analogue signals or high-speed digital boards, and pick the experience you put in your application to match.

ROLE_ANALYSIS_V1.summary: Predicting performance with an analysis model before anything is built, and stating how far that prediction can be trusted
ROLE_ANALYSIS_V1.practiceWhere: in electromagnetics or signal processing coursework or simulation work in a research lab

TD06.why: Predicting how antennas, transmission lines and RF circuits behave with an electromagnetic field solver is where analysis roles are used most.
TD06.ctx: in electromagnetics, antenna or microwave course projects

out.J4: Note on the simulation model and boundary conditions
out.J6: Simulated versus measured return loss table

TD04.why: Handling signals and noise with numerical models lets you estimate how well a processing method will perform before you measure anything.
TD04.ctx: in numerical assignments in a signal processing course

TD08.why: Calculating losses and heating in power circuits ahead of time produces results that become the basis for design changes.
TD08.ctx: when you simulate a converter circuit in a power electronics course

out.J6: Calculated loss versus measured efficiency table

J1.task: Before you start, write one question this analysis will answer (for example, is this antenna matched in the target band) and the effects you will leave out.
J1.check: Is the question written as a single sentence?

J2.task: Turn that question into analysis conditions, writing the frequency range, input conditions and the metrics you will judge by (return loss, gain, losses and so on) as numbers.
J2.check: Does every metric have a target value?

J3.task: Decide yourself how far to simplify the model, and for each structure or effect you remove, write one line on how it affects the result.
J3.check: Does each removed item have a reason why removing it is acceptable?

J4.task: Run the model at two or three mesh sizes or time steps, and use the setting beyond which the result stops changing.
J4.check: Did you record how much the result changed with the mesh?

J5.task: Put the model files, analysis conditions and tool versions in one document so the next person can get the same result.
J5.check: Could someone rerun the same analysis from the report alone?

J6.task: Compare your results with lab measurements or textbook formulas under the same conditions.
J6.check: Are the ranges that differ and the likely reasons written down?

J7.task: When simulation and measurement differ a lot, check the model, boundary conditions and measurement one at a time, find where they part ways and reset the conditions.
J7.check: Are the order of checks and the conditions you changed written down?

J8.task: If your team changed dimensions or component values based on your results, record what changed and why.
J8.output: Record of how the analysis was used
J8.check: Does it say which result was used for which design change?

responsibilities: Predicting the electrical, electromagnetic and thermal behaviour of proposed designs
Building analysis models and conditions and documenting simplifying assumptions
Comparing analysis with test measurements and calibrating models
Writing analysis reports and providing the basis for design changes

process.what: Design asks questions such as whether this structure can hit the band, or how hot this power supply will get.
You enter the geometry and material properties and set the boundary conditions and how far to simplify.
You vary the mesh or time step to find where the result settles.
You run the analysis, judge whether it meets the target metrics, and look at how each design variable affects the result.
When prototype measurements come in, you compare them with the analysis and calibrate the model.
You hand the results to design together with the range over which they can be trusted.

tools: Circuit simulators (SPICE family)
Electromagnetic solvers (finite element and time-domain methods)
Numerical computing tools (MATLAB or Python)
How to read vector network analyser measurements
experiences: Matching simulation results with measurements
Simplifying a model and working out the effect of doing so
Documenting analysis settings so someone else could rerun them
entry: Solve electromagnetics or antenna coursework with a simulation tool and compare with the textbook formulas
Join a simulation-focused lab as an undergraduate research assistant and take on one model
In your capstone, produce predicted values by simulation before the prototype is built

learnOrder.why: If you know the rough answer, you notice when a simulation result looks wrong.
Each tool sets up conditions differently, and knowing one well makes it easier to move to another.
Whether you can trust a simulation comes down to these two.
An analysis that has never been checked against measurement is hard to use as evidence.

firstProject.title: Simulate a patch antenna and match it to measurements
firstProject.goal: Design a patch antenna for a target frequency from the formulas, and explain the difference in resonant frequency between simulation and measurement
steps: Choose a target frequency and calculate the patch dimensions with the textbook formulas
Build the model in an electromagnetic solver and vary the mesh until the return loss settles
Make the board in the lab and measure it with a vector network analyser, or if you cannot measure, run the simulation two different ways and compare them
Summarise on one page the resonant frequency from formula, simulation and measurement, and why they differ
firstProject.output: Analysis conditions table, mesh convergence record and a one-page three-way comparison table
firstProject.check: Can you explain which model assumption accounts for the gap between simulation and measurement?

portfolio: A report setting out the analysis model and conditions
A table comparing simulated and measured values
One page on the range over which you trust the results and their limits

interview.q: How did you choose the mesh and boundary conditions? How did you confirm they were right?
interview.why: How you set the conditions shows whether you understand the analysis better than the result does.

interview.q: Have your simulation and measurement ever disagreed? How did you explain the difference?
interview.why: An analysis role is accountable for whether the predictions hold.

interview.q: What did you deliberately leave out of the model, and why did you think that was acceptable?
interview.why: What you choose to simplify decides the quality of an analysis.

postingCheck: Whether the analysis is electromagnetic, circuit or thermal
Whether experience with a specific tool is required or only preferred
Whether the job is analysis only or includes design or test
ROLE_ANALYSIS_V1.watch: Dedicated analysis roles, often titled Simulation Engineer, RF Simulation Engineer or Signal Integrity Engineer, tend to sit in research centres and large development organisations, and many postings ask for a master's degree. If you are graduating with a bachelor's degree, it is realistic to also look at design or test roles that include analysis work.

ROLE_TEST_V1.summary: Setting up test procedures to measure whether a product or module meets its specifications and standards, and making sure the verdict comes out the same when the test is repeated
ROLE_TEST_V1.practiceWhere: in electronic circuits or instrumentation labs or when evaluating your capstone prototype

TD12.why: Turning the test items in a standard into measurement conditions and acceptance criteria, and working out measurement uncertainty, is the core of a test role.
TD12.ctx: in an instrumentation lab or a prototype performance evaluation

TD02.why: Confirming with a testbench that digital logic works in every case is a separate job in chip and FPGA development, with dedicated verification engineers.
TD02.ctx: in a digital design course or FPGA lab

out.J4: Testbench and list of test cases
out.J6: Results checked against a reference model

TD05.why: Measuring the data rate and error rate of a communication module on a test network and judging them against the limits in the standard.
TD05.ctx: in a communications lab or a project that uses a wireless module

out.J6: Measurement table against the standard's limits

J1.task: At the top of the test plan, write what is being tested and what this test will not cover (for example, long-term life).
J1.check: Are the excluded items listed with the reason for excluding them?

J2.task: Turn the requirements in the project specification or datasheet into test items, measurement conditions (input, load, temperature) and acceptance criteria.
J2.check: Does every item have its conditions and limit value together?

J3.task: Set the limit that separates pass from fail yourself, and write how much allowance for measurement error you built into the specified value.
J3.check: Can you explain why you put the limit where you did?

J4.task: Check the resolution and accuracy of your instruments, measure the same item with two instruments or methods, and decide which to use.
J4.check: Are the limits of the instrument you chose written down?

J5.task: Write a test procedure with the connection diagram, instrument settings and measurement order so a teammate following it gets the same values.
J5.check: Did someone else reproduce the test from the procedure alone?

J6.task: Measure the same item several times, calculate the spread, and make the pass or fail call looking at both the mean and the spread.
J6.output: Repeat measurement results and verdict table
J6.check: Did the verdict take the spread into account?

J7.task: When measurements are unstable, work out whether the sample, the instrument or the procedure is the cause, decide the conditions for remeasuring and retest.
J7.check: Is the reason for changing the retest conditions written down?

J8.task: Record what design fixed after seeing your test results, or whether they moved on to the next stage.
J8.output: Record of how verdicts were used
J8.check: Does it say which decision the test results fed into?

responsibilities: Writing test plans and setting test items and acceptance criteria
Writing test procedures and setting up the test environment
Running performance, environmental and EMC tests and writing test reports
Supporting root cause analysis of failed items and retesting

process.what: The product specification, the standards that apply and customer requirements arrive along with the item to test.
You set the test items, measurement conditions, acceptance criteria and number of samples.
You choose instruments, check their calibration, and set up connections and settings.
You measure by the procedure and record the spread of repeat measurements alongside.
You compare the results with the criteria, make the call and issue the test report.
You narrow down the cause of failed items with design and test again after the fix.

tools: Oscilloscope, spectrum analyser and digital multimeter
Measurement automation scripts (Python and similar)
HDL simulators and testbenches
How to read EMC standards (the IEC 61000 series and CISPR standards)
experiences: Writing a test procedure that someone else reproduced
Making a pass or fail call from repeat measurement results
Finding the cause of unstable measurements and retesting
entry: In your circuits and instrumentation lab reports, include repeat measurement results with their spread
Take on prototype performance evaluation and the test plan in your capstone team
Pick the datasheet of a part you are interested in and tabulate the conditions under which each specification was measured

learnOrder.why: If you do not know an instrument's limits, you cannot justify a verdict.
The first job in a test plan is turning requirements into conditions you can measure.
Calls near the limit can only be made if you know the uncertainty.
To run the same test the same way many times, a script beats doing it by hand.

firstProject.title: Verify the output specifications of one DC power module yourself
firstProject.goal: Measure the output voltage, ripple and efficiency listed in the datasheet of an off-the-shelf DC-DC converter module and judge whether it meets them
steps: Find the output specification items and their measurement conditions in the datasheet and put them in a test items table
Write a procedure with the measurement order and instrument settings for several load steps
Measure each item several times and calculate the mean and spread
Compare with the specification, make the call, and for items near the limit set retest conditions and measure again
firstProject.output: Test items table, test procedure, verdict table and retest record
firstProject.check: Could someone else reach the same verdict from your procedure alone?

portfolio: A test plan and test report as one set
A verdict table that accounts for the spread of repeat measurements
One page on which conditions you retested under and why

interview.q: Have you measured the same thing several times and got different values? How did you decide pass or fail?
interview.why: Testing means making a call from values that scatter.

interview.q: Have you written down a test procedure for someone else to follow?
interview.why: A test report is only evidence if the verdict can be reproduced.

interview.q: Have you remeasured because readings were unstable? What did you change?
interview.why: How you set retest conditions shows whether you habitually isolate causes.

postingCheck: Whether you would test at chip, board or finished product level
Whether the focus is performance testing or certification testing such as EMC and reliability
For digital verification roles, whether the posting names the hardware description language and verification methods it expects
ROLE_TEST_V1.watch: The same word, verification, means checking logic in code in chip development and measuring performance with instruments for finished products. A Design Verification Engineer and a Test Engineer do very different work, so read the duties and preferred skills in the posting and work out which one it is first.

ROLE_PROCESS_V1.summary: Setting process conditions and control criteria so what design specified comes out the same however many are made, and steadily reducing defects
ROLE_PROCESS_V1.practiceWhere: in a semiconductor process lab or a project that involves PCB fabrication and assembly

TD07.why: Setting the process sequence and conditions that achieve the device characteristics and watching the yield is the core of a process role.
TD07.ctx: in a semiconductor engineering course or a process lab

out.J6: Characteristics before and after a condition change

TD12.why: Deciding what to inspect in production and how many is where you confirm in numbers that process conditions are being held.
TD12.ctx: when you gather lab data and plot it on a control chart

out.J4: Diagram of the inspection data flow

TD02.why: At the boundary where chip design data is handed to the process, you check that the design rules and process capability match.
TD02.ctx: when you look at synthesis and place-and-route results in a digital design course

J1.task: Write the target characteristics of the samples you will make in the lab, and separate the process variables you will change this time from those you will hold fixed.
J1.check: Does it list which variables you held fixed?

J2.task: Turn the target characteristics (film thickness, sheet resistance, threshold voltage and so on) into control criteria with upper and lower limits.
J2.check: Does every item have a target value and upper and lower limits?

J3.task: Set one condition yourself, such as deposition time, anneal temperature or soldering temperature, and write why you chose that value and rejected the others.
J3.check: Is the basis for the value kept in your measurement data?

J4.task: Measure several samples made under the same conditions, plot a control chart, and find the point where the trend shifted.
J4.check: Did you mark points outside the control limits or drifting to one side?

J5.task: Make a process conditions sheet with the sequence, settings and cautions so a teammate following it produces the same sample.
J5.check: Did someone else make the same sample from the sheet alone?

J6.task: Calculate the defect rate or characteristic distribution before and after a condition change with the same measurement method, and compare.
J6.check: Are the number of samples and the measurement method written alongside?

J7.task: Pick a defect that kept appearing, narrow the cause to equipment, material, conditions or work method, and change the conditions or sequence so it does not come back.
J7.output: Defect cause and recurrence prevention record
J7.check: Did you check again that the same defect dropped after the change?

J8.task: If your conditions sheet was used as it is by another group or in the next lab session, record that.
J8.output: Record of how the conditions sheet was used
J8.check: Does it say who used the sheet for which build?

responsibilities: Setting process conditions and reviewing process changes
Analysing yield and defect data and making improvements
Setting process control criteria and inspection items
Finalising process conditions and writing work instructions when new products move to production

process.what: Drawings and target characteristics for a new product come over from design.
You run trial production, set the process conditions and put control limits on them.
You release the conditions sheet and work instructions to the line and watch early quality.
You collect inspection data and yield every day and watch for shifts in the trend.
When defects rise, you narrow down the cause, adjust the conditions and confirm the effect.
You write the revised conditions into the work instructions for the next run.

tools: Spreadsheets and statistics tools (control charts, distribution plots)
How to read semiconductor parameter analyser results
Templates for process conditions sheets and work instructions
Defect cause tools (fishbone diagrams, Pareto charts)
experiences: Changing a process condition and confirming the difference by measurement
Analysing the spread of samples made under the same conditions
Narrowing down a defect cause and stopping it from coming back
entry: Take a course with a semiconductor process lab and organise your measurements by condition in tables and distributions
In a project where you order and assemble your own PCBs, collect the assembly defects and sort them by cause
Calculate control charts and process capability indices yourself in an engineering statistics or quality control course

learnOrder.why: You can only adjust conditions if you know which process step changes which characteristic.
Process work means spotting anomalies in data that builds up every day.
A defect report is read for how you ruled out candidate causes.
If you change several variables at once, you cannot tell which one had the effect.

firstProject.title: Make the same sample many times and reduce the spread
firstProject.goal: Pick a sample you make in the lab (a thin film, a resistor pattern, a solder joint and so on), make several under the same conditions, and find one condition that reduces the spread
steps: Set the target characteristic and tolerance, and separate the one variable you will change from those you will hold fixed
Make several under the same conditions, measure them and plot the distribution and a control chart
Change the one variable, make another batch and compare the before and after distributions with the same method
Write the better condition into a conditions sheet and check that a teammate following it gets the same result
firstProject.output: Control criteria table, before and after distribution comparison and a one-page process conditions sheet
firstProject.check: Can you explain the effect of the condition change with numbers from the distributions?

portfolio: A process conditions sheet with the reasons behind each condition
A table comparing defect rates or distributions before and after a condition change
One page on the action that stopped a recurring defect

interview.q: Have you set or changed a process condition yourself? How did you choose the value?
interview.why: A process role sets condition values and takes responsibility for them.

interview.q: After changing a condition, how did you show it really improved?
interview.why: Whether you compared before and after under the same conditions shows the quality of your judgement.

interview.q: What did you change so the same problem would not happen again?
interview.why: In production you spend more time preventing recurrence than making one-off fixes.

postingCheck: Whether the process is front-end (wafer fabrication), back-end (packaging and test) or board assembly
Whether the role involves shift work or being based on the production line
Whether statistics or design of experiments experience, or specific process names, are listed as a plus
ROLE_PROCESS_V1.watch: Process engineers often work close to the production line, so check the location and working pattern in the posting first. These roles, often titled Process Engineer, Process Integration Engineer or Yield Engineer, are frequently shared with materials and chemistry graduates. As an electrical and electronic engineering graduate, show in your application how you used circuit knowledge in measurement and defect analysis.

ROLE_MAINT_V1.summary: Setting operating and inspection criteria so power and automation equipment does not stop, and finding the cause and restoring it when it fails
ROLE_MAINT_V1.practiceWhere: in electrical machines or automatic control labs or during an industry internship

TD09.why: Operating and inspecting substations, motors and protective relays is the area equipment maintenance roles spend longest in.
TD09.ctx: in electrical machines or power engineering labs

out.J3: Inspection interval and replacement criteria table
out.J7: Record of narrowing down a fault cause

TD11.why: Working with production equipment driven by PLCs and servo drives means fault response often starts with the control sequence and the sensors.
TD11.ctx: in an automatic control or PLC lab

TD10.why: Setting operating limits and inspection criteria for energy equipment that runs all the time, such as solar and energy storage systems.
TD10.ctx: in a renewable energy course or when you look at generation equipment on campus

J1.task: Pick one piece of lab equipment (a motor drive panel, a PLC trainer and so on) and write what you will inspect this time and what you will leave out.
J1.check: Does it list the parts you leave out and why?

J2.task: Read the equipment ratings and manual and write its operating limits, such as current, temperature and insulation resistance, as numbers.
J2.check: Does every value have its source (rating, manual or regulation)?

J3.task: Set an interval and replacement criterion for each inspection item yourself, and write one line on why.
J3.check: Can you explain why you made the interval neither shorter nor longer?

J4.task: Log current or temperature during operation, plot it, and decide how you will pick out signals that differ from normal.
J4.output: Operating log chart and note on the judging method
J4.check: Does it say how you set the normal range?

J5.task: Make an inspection log template the next person can read and continue from, and actually fill it in.
J5.check: Are date, readings, action and person responsible all filled in?

J6.task: Put the insulation resistance or running current you measured next to the limit and past records, and judge the condition of the equipment.
J6.check: Are the criteria and past values you used shown together?

J7.task: Take one fault or malfunction you hit in the lab, narrow it down step by step to wiring, settings or the device, and write the recovery procedure.
J7.check: Are the order of checks and the post-recovery function check written down?

J8.task: If your inspection records or verdicts were used to decide on a part replacement or settings change, record what happened.
J8.output: Record of how maintenance judgements were used
J8.check: Does it say which judgement led to which action?

responsibilities: Operating and routinely inspecting substations, distribution equipment, motors and automation equipment
Setting inspection intervals and replacement criteria and planning preventive maintenance
Analysing fault causes, restoring equipment and preventing recurrence
Electrical safety management and keeping inspection records

process.what: You read the single-line diagrams, sequence diagrams and ratings for your equipment and confirm its operating limits.
You set inspection items, intervals and replacement criteria and turn them into a schedule.
You log operating data and measure and inspect at the set intervals.
You look for current, temperature or sound that differs from normal and act before the equipment stops.
You narrow down why the equipment stopped, restore it and record the stoppage and recovery.
You look at the fault history and reset inspection intervals and replacement criteria.

knowledge: Electrical installation codes and regulations in your country
tools: Insulation resistance tester, clamp meter and multimeter
PLC programming tools (ladder diagrams)
How to read single-line and sequence diagrams
Inspection with a thermal imaging camera
experiences: Inspecting equipment yourself and keeping records
Narrowing down the cause of a fault or malfunction step by step
Reading ratings and manuals and setting operating limits
entry: In electrical machines and sequence control labs, keep your wiring and measurement records as an inspection log
Organise your coursework in electrical machines, power engineering and installation codes around the syllabus of an entry-level electrical licence, where your country has one
During a summer internship, watch operation and inspection work up close in a plant or a building's electrical room

learnOrder.why: Understanding equipment starts with reading its drawings.

learnOrder.step: Using meters and following safety rules
learnOrder.why: Maintenance often means working next to live equipment.
You can only find faults in automation equipment if you can read the sequence.
With records built up, you can change inspection intervals with evidence.

firstProject.title: Build an inspection criteria table for one piece of lab equipment
firstProject.goal: Pick a motor drive panel or PLC trainer in your department's lab, set its operating limits and inspection criteria, and keep records for a semester
steps: With permission from the professor or lab technician, collect the equipment's ratings, manual and wiring diagram and tabulate its operating limits
Set inspection items, intervals and replacement criteria and write down why
Measure current, temperature and insulation resistance at the set intervals and fill in the inspection log
Look at the records you built up, choose the criteria that should change and propose revisions
firstProject.output: Operating limits table, inspection criteria table, a filled-in inspection log and proposed revisions
firstProject.check: Can you explain why you proposed changing a criterion with numbers from the records?

portfolio: A table of inspection criteria and intervals
A record of narrowing down a fault cause and restoring the equipment
One page of operating limits with their sources

interview.q: When equipment or a circuit suddenly stopped, in what order did you look for the cause?
interview.why: In maintenance, the order for bringing stopped equipment back has to be second nature.

interview.q: Have you set an inspection interval or replacement criterion? What did you base it on?
interview.why: Whether you set criteria with evidence shows the depth of your judgement.

interview.q: Have you kept records so the next person could take over?
interview.why: Maintenance means several people looking after the same equipment in turn.

postingCheck: Whether the equipment is mainly substations and distribution or production automation
Whether an electrical licence is required, and whether the role is tied to a legally designated electrical safety position
Whether there is shift work or on-call duty
ROLE_MAINT_V1.watch: Many equipment maintenance postings, often titled Electrical Maintenance Engineer or Facilities Electrical Engineer, require or prefer an electrical licence. In many countries the law requires larger sites to appoint a qualified person responsible for electrical safety, and the requirements depend on the size of the installation. If a role interests you, read the qualifications in the posting together with the relevant parts of your country's electrical safety rules.

ROLE_PM_V1.summary: Setting requirements, scope, schedule and roles so parts built by several teams come together as one system, and resolving the mismatches
ROLE_PM_V1.practiceWhere: in your capstone design or a team build project

TD11.why: Aligning the conditions between subsystems in a system where sensors, controllers and actuators interlock is where technical planning is most often needed.
TD11.ctx: when you bring several modules together in your capstone

out.J8: Integration test results and agreement record

TD05.why: Setting the data and communication protocols that devices exchange is where the interface documents between teams come from.
TD05.ctx: in a project where several devices communicate

TD10.why: Setting the scope of equipment configuration and operating strategy for energy systems that combine generation, storage and load.
TD10.ctx: in a renewable energy design project or competition

J1.task: At the start of a project, write on one page the scope of the system you will build and the features you will not do this semester, and get your teammates and supervisor to confirm it.
J1.check: Are the features you will not do listed with the reasons?

J2.task: Collect the requirements from teammates, your supervisor and users, turn them into numeric conditions and rank them.
J2.check: Does every requirement have a way to verify it and a priority?

J3.task: When time runs short, decide yourself which features stay and which go, and write how dropping each one affects the system.
J3.check: Can you explain to your teammates why you dropped each feature?

J4.task: Choose a scheduling method that suits your team, such as a Gantt chart or work breakdown structure, use it, and note why you chose it.
J4.check: Does every task have an owner and a due date?

J5.task: Write the signals, voltages and communication formats exchanged between modules into an interface definition, and keep a change history every time it changes.
J5.check: Can you see from the history who changed what, when and why?

J6.task: Before integration, check each module's actual outputs against the interface definition.
J6.check: Are mismatched items and their owners listed in the table?

J7.task: Narrow down why the schedule slipped or integration failed, and share with the team how you reset the scope or schedule.
J7.check: Do you have evidence that narrows the slip to one cause?

J8.task: Record whether the requirements definition or interface definition you wrote became the basis for your teammates' work.
J8.output: Record of how the documents were used
J8.check: Does it say which teammate used the document for which task?

responsibilities: Defining product and system requirements and writing technical specifications
Planning development schedule and resources and tracking progress
Coordinating interfaces between departments and managing changes
Planning integration tests, reporting results and handling customer requirements

process.what: You collect requirements from customers, sales and design and sort out the ones that overlap or conflict.
You decide what to build, what to drop and the priorities, and get agreement from the departments involved.
You break the work down and attach owners, schedule and the resources needed.
You document the conditions exchanged between subsystems and keep a history every time they change.
You bring the modules together, test them and check them against the requirements.
When the schedule slips or requirements change, you reset the scope and schedule.

knowledge: Basic systems engineering (requirements definition, interface management)
Basics of control engineering and communications engineering
Core concepts across the main fields of electrical and electronic engineering
tools: Scheduling methods (Gantt charts, work breakdown structures)
Requirements traceability tables and change history
Collaboration tools and version control
Tools for drawing block diagrams and system architecture diagrams
experiences: Organising requirements and scope on a team project and getting agreement
Finding and resolving mismatches between modules
Resetting the scope when the schedule slipped
entry: Take on team lead or integration in your capstone design and write the requirements and interface definitions
Enter an engineering competition and manage the schedule and change history through to the end
Read the public specification of a product you are interested in and draw a block diagram that splits it into submodules

learnOrder.why: Integration starts with drawing the boundaries between subsystems.
A requirement without numbers can be neither agreed nor verified.
Planning means deciding what stays when there is not enough time.
If nobody records who changed what and why, the same arguments repeat at integration.

firstProject.title: Build a set of requirements and interface documents for your capstone system
firstProject.goal: Pick one team project and manage the requirements definition, block diagram, interface definition and change history for a whole semester
steps: Collect requirements from teammates and your supervisor into a requirements table with numeric conditions and priorities
Draw a block diagram that splits the system into modules, and write the signal, power and communication conditions between modules into a definition document
Every time something changes, record the date, what changed and why in the change history
At integration testing, check every requirement and write up why any items were not met
firstProject.output: Requirements table, block diagram and interface definition, change history and requirements check table
firstProject.check: From the change history alone, can you explain why the final result differs from the original plan?

portfolio: One page of requirements and priorities
An interface definition that aligned the conditions between modules
A change history and a record of resetting the scope

interview.q: When requirements conflicted, how did you set priorities and get agreement?
interview.why: Technical planning is the role that sorts out conflicting requirements.

interview.q: When you could not finish everything in time, what did you cut? Why that?
interview.why: What you cut shows your criteria for judgement.

interview.q: Has a document you wrote become the basis for someone else's work?
interview.why: Planning deliverables become useful when other people work from them.

postingCheck: Whether technical planning here centres on defining product requirements or on managing projects and programmes
Whether hands-on experience in a particular area (control, communications, energy and so on) is required
Whether the posting says what graduates would handle (gathering data, managing schedules and so on)
ROLE_PM_V1.watch: Technical planning and integration roles, often titled Systems Engineer or Technical Project Manager, are usually filled by people moving across after design or test experience, so there are relatively few graduate openings. It is realistic to also consider starting in a design or test role and taking on integration work there.

ROLE_RND_V1.summary: Narrowing down a technical question that has no settled answer yet, and deciding by experiment and calculation whether it works
ROLE_RND_V1.practiceWhere: as an undergraduate research assistant or in a final-year thesis or capstone research project

TD07.why: Checking first whether a new device structure or process condition can deliver the target characteristics, an area with a lot of advanced research.
TD07.ctx: in a semiconductor devices course or sample experiments in a research lab

out.J5: Record of experimental method and conditions

TD04.why: Proposing a new processing method and comparing it with existing ones on the same data is an area undergraduates can start in without large equipment.
TD04.ctx: in signal processing coursework or research using public datasets

TD06.why: Drawing the line, by simulation and measurement, on the conditions a new antenna or RF structure can handle.
TD06.ctx: in projects in an electromagnetics or microwave research lab

out.J7: Table of the conditions that limit where it applies

J1.task: Pick a question in your area of interest that has no answer yet, and narrow what you need to find out down to one sentence.
J1.output: One-sentence research question with a scope note
J1.check: Is the question narrow enough to answer with one experiment or calculation?

J2.task: Turn the question into conditions you can check, writing what you will measure and what value would count as success.
J2.check: Is there a threshold that separates works from does not work?

J3.task: List the assumptions you made, and for each one write how the result changes if it breaks.
J3.output: List of assumptions and the conditions that break them
J3.check: Does every assumption have the condition under which it breaks?

J4.task: Find at least two methods in papers or textbooks and compare them, and if none fits, record why you adapted an existing method.
J4.check: Can you explain the limits of the methods you did not choose?

J5.task: Keep the code, experimental conditions and raw data in one place so someone else can get the same result.
J5.check: Did someone else reproduce your result from the materials alone?

J6.task: Put experimental and calculated values side by side under the same conditions, and write where they differ and why.
J6.check: Did you check the candidate reasons for the gap one by one?

J7.task: Vary the conditions to find where your proposed method stops performing, and draw the line.
J7.output: Record of the limits where it applies
J7.check: Is the condition value at the limit written down?

J8.task: Record where your results went: a conference talk, your thesis, a lab report or the next experiment plan.
J8.output: Record of how results were used
J8.check: Does it say which next-stage decision the results fed into?

responsibilities: Feasibility studies and early experiments on new devices and approaches
Technology trend research and paper and patent searches
Building prototypes and test samples and evaluating performance
Writing research reports, supporting patent filings and transferring technology to development

process.what: A technical question with no answer yet comes in from product planning or a research project.
You search papers and patents and separate what is already known from what is left.
You set the assumptions and decision criteria, and decide what to hold fixed and what to vary.
You make samples or models, measure them and compare with calculations.
You vary the conditions to separate the range where the method holds from where it does not.
You write up the results as reports, patents or prototypes and hand them to development.

knowledge: Advanced courses in your area of interest (semiconductor devices, signal processing, electromagnetics and so on)
tools: Numerical computing and programming tools (MATLAB or Python)
Field-specific simulators (device, electromagnetic, circuit)
Academic databases and patent databases such as Google Patents or Espacenet
Lab notebooks and version control
experiences: Narrowing an open question and checking it by experiment
Reproducing a paper's results yourself
Writing down the limits of a method you proposed as conditions
entry: Join a lab you are interested in as an undergraduate research assistant and reproduce one of a senior student's experiments
Pick one result figure from a paper in your area and redraw it from your own calculations or experiments
Submit your results to an undergraduate research competition or a student session at a conference

learnOrder.step: Reproducing one paper all the way through
learnOrder.why: Reproducing a paper shows you the conditions it did not write down.
Advanced research succeeds or fails on how well the question is narrowed.
The next person can only use a result if you also write how far it holds.
Advanced research roles are often entered through a graduate degree, so it helps to make that decision early.

firstProject.title: Reproduce a paper's result and look for its limits
firstProject.goal: Pick a paper in your area, reproduce one of its main results, and find one condition under which the method does not hold
steps: Write the paper's question, assumptions and evaluation metrics on one page
Recreate one result figure using public data or samples and models you make yourself
Find where your result differs from the paper's and write down why
Vary one condition to find where performance drops off, and draw the line
firstProject.output: One page of questions and assumptions, reproduction results with a comparison table, and a record of limiting conditions
firstProject.check: Can you give at least one limiting condition the paper did not mention, with evidence?

portfolio: A research report setting out the question, assumptions and limits
Materials describing methods and conditions so someone else can rerun them
A table comparing your values with those from a different method

interview.q: How did you narrow down a problem that had no set answer before you started?
interview.why: Advanced research starts with framing the question.

interview.q: What did you do when there was no suitable method?
interview.why: This role often calls for adapting existing methods or building new ones.

interview.q: Have you checked where a method you proposed stops working?
interview.why: The next person trusts results from someone who looked for the limits themselves.

postingCheck: How the degree requirement (bachelor's, master's, PhD) is worded
Whether the research topic is in devices, circuits, signals or communications
Whether a record of papers or patents is required or preferred
ROLE_RND_V1.watch: Advanced R&D postings, often titled Research Engineer or R&D Engineer, commonly require a master's or PhD. If you want this kind of role as an undergraduate, build lab experience early and think seriously about graduate school.

ROLE_QUALITY_V1.summary: Assuring through set criteria that a product meets its requirements throughout production and throughout its service life, and following corrective action through to the end when problems appear
ROLE_QUALITY_V1.practiceWhere: in quality control or reliability courses or durability testing of a prototype

TD12.why: Judging from production data and test results whether criteria are exceeded is the area quality roles deal with every day.
TD12.ctx: when you collect instrumentation lab data and make verdicts from it

TD07.why: Dealing with defects and life of semiconductor devices is where failure analysis and accelerated testing happen.
TD07.ctx: in a semiconductor devices course or sample evaluation experiments

TD09.why: Judging insulation ageing and life of electrical machines and power equipment, where the longer equipment is in service, the more reliability judgements come with it.
TD09.ctx: in an electrical machines lab or insulation testing lab

J1.task: Pick a prototype or lab sample and separate the quality items you will assure this time from those you will not cover.
J1.check: Are the items you do not cover listed with the reasons?

J2.task: Turn a user requirement such as it does not shut off when left on for a long time into a quality criterion you can measure.
J2.check: Does every criterion have a measurement method and an acceptance range?

J3.task: Set accelerated conditions with raised temperature or voltage and the life judgement criteria yourself, and write how those conditions relate to real use.
J3.output: Note on accelerated conditions and criteria
J3.check: Did you explain how the accelerated conditions relate to real use?

J4.task: Sort the defect data you collected by symptom, location and process, draw a Pareto chart, and decide which candidate causes to look at first.
J4.output: Defect classification table and Pareto chart
J4.check: Is there a reason for the causes you chose to look at first?

J5.task: Make and fill in a corrective action record so the problem, cause, action and verification can be followed afterwards.
J5.check: Is the effect check after the action filled in too?

J6.task: Set the distribution of measurements from several samples against the criteria, calculate a process capability index, and judge whether it meets them.
J6.check: Are the number of samples and the formula you used written down?

J7.task: Decide an action to stop the same defect recurring, and check with samples made after the action whether it really dropped.
J7.check: Did you compare before and after against the same criteria?

J8.task: If your verdicts or action records were used for a team submission decision or the next build, record what happened.
J8.output: Record of how verdicts were used
J8.check: Does it say which verdict led to which decision?

responsibilities: Setting quality criteria and making outgoing inspection calls
Planning reliability tests and assessing life
Analysing defects and tracking corrective action
Handling customer quality enquiries and managing quality system documents

process.what: Customer requirements, applicable standards and internal criteria arrive with a new product.
You set the quality items, acceptance criteria and reliability test conditions.
Reliability tests and early production inspection confirm whether the criteria are met.
You watch the trend in production data and look for signs that criteria are about to be exceeded.
When a defect appears, you narrow down the cause, set corrective action and confirm the effect.
Based on the verdict, you hold or release shipments and record the reasons.

knowledge: Quality control and engineering statistics (control charts, process capability indices)
Reliability engineering (failure rate, life distributions, accelerated testing)
Basics of semiconductor devices and electronic circuits
tools: Statistics tools and spreadsheets (distributions, control charts, Weibull analysis)
How to operate environmental test equipment for temperature and humidity
How to read reliability test standards (JEDEC and IEC test standards)
Corrective action report templates (8D reports and similar)
experiences: Making a pass or fail call from measurement data
Narrowing down a defect cause and confirming that the action worked
Recording corrective action and following it through to the end
entry: Calculate control charts and process capability indices yourself in a quality control or engineering statistics course
Build several capstone prototypes and run a simple durability test, running them for a long time at different temperatures
Organise your quality control knowledge around the syllabus of a recognised quality engineering certification

learnOrder.why: Quality verdicts are made from distributions rather than single values.
A defect report is read for how you narrowed down the cause.
Life is hard to measure by waiting for failure, so it is estimated with accelerated tests and distributions.
Customers and certification bodies check verdicts through documents.

firstProject.title: Run a small reliability test on a few prototypes
firstProject.goal: Build several identical circuit boards, run them for a long time at different temperatures, judge them against criteria, and record the cause and action for any failure
steps: Write down the conditions of use and set the quality items to watch and the acceptance criteria
Set test conditions with raised temperature or supply voltage and a test duration, and write down why
Measure the characteristics at set intervals and record the distribution and how it changes
If any board exceeds the criteria, narrow down the cause, test again after the action and record the result
firstProject.output: Quality criteria table, test conditions note, measurement records and corrective action record
firstProject.check: Can you explain the test conditions and verdicts in terms of real conditions of use?

portfolio: A table of quality criteria and the basis for each verdict
A corrective action record covering cause, action and effect check
One page on the accelerated conditions used for the life judgement

interview.q: Have you judged pass or fail from measurement data? What did you base it on?
interview.why: A quality role makes the call and explains its basis.

interview.q: What did you do so the same problem would not happen again, and how did you confirm it really dropped?
interview.why: The persistence quality work needs shows in confirming the effect, more than in the action itself.

interview.q: Has your judgement ever delayed a schedule or changed a plan?
interview.why: A quality role sometimes has to make the call to stop a shipment.

postingCheck: Whether the role covers incoming, process or outgoing quality, or is dedicated to reliability testing
Whether customer quality handling is part of the job
Whether quality certifications or statistics tool experience are listed as a plus
ROLE_QUALITY_V1.watch: Quality engineers, often titled Quality Engineer, Reliability Engineer or Supplier Quality Engineer, frequently have to explain verdicts between process and test teams and customers. Some industries, such as automotive electronics, follow industry-specific quality standards (IATF 16949, the AEC-Q series and so on), so once you have a target industry, look up the names of its standards first.
